questions.q: Why can three teams report three different revenue numbers from the same Opportunity table?
options: Salesforce randomly changes stored values
Each team applied its own logic, such as which stages count and whether refunds are netted, because the raw table carries no business definition
The Opportunity object only stores one record
Dashboards always round numbers differently
questions.explain: Raw tables have columns but not business meaning. Without a shared definition, each team encodes its own logic.

questions.q: Where does a semantic layer sit in the analytics stack?
options: Between the data layer and the consumers such as dashboards and AI assistants
Inside each individual dashboard
Only inside the browser
Below the raw storage, replacing it
questions.explain: The layer sits between data and consumers, translating raw tables into governed business meaning that every consumer reuses.

questions.q: Which is Salesforce's implementation of a semantic layer?
options: A Reports list view
A Flow
A validation rule
The semantic model, built in the Semantic Model Builder and powered by Tableau Semantics
questions.explain: Semantic models are built with the Semantic Model Builder in Tableau Next and Data 360.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which items make up a semantic model?
options: Page layouts, record types, and profiles
Data objects, relationships, calculated fields, and metrics
Only a single flat table
Apex triggers and Visualforce pages
questions.explain: A semantic model combines data objects (DMOs, DLOs, calculated insights), relationships, calculated fields, and metrics.

questions.q: Why do semantic layers matter even more when AI assistants answer questions?
options: AI assistants cannot read data at all
AI needs no context, so the layer is unnecessary
Defined business meaning gives assistants the context to answer consistently instead of guessing from column names
Semantic layers make AI responses slower on purpose
questions.explain: Business definitions such as what counts as Open Pipeline give conversational analytics the context to answer consistently.
